# Churchill Downs Stakes Recaps: Mercante Wires Field in Grade III, $300,000 River City; Viking Boldly Raids $300,000 Bet On Sunshine


## Nov 07, 2026


Carl Pollard’s 6-year-old homebred gelding Mercante went straight to the front and outlasted a constant threat from 2-1 favorite Kupuna to prevail in Saturday’s 47th running of the $300,000 River City (Grade III) at Churchill Downs by a half-length.


The victory, clocked in 1:47.20 for 1 1/8 miles on firm turn with the rails 12-feet out, gave 28-year-old jockey Walter Rodriguez his first career graded stakes win and first stakes victory beneath Churchill Downs’ historic Twin Spires. The native of El Salvador rode the winner for trainer Brian Knippenberg.


“It was very special to get this win today and I can’t thank Brian and Mr. Carl Pollard enough,” Rodriguez said. “I know from riding him this winter at Turfway (to a second-place finish in the Grade III TwinSpires Kentucky Cup Classic) how nice of a horse he is. He’s a very classy horse in the mornings and in the afternoon.”


Breaking from post No. 2 in the compact field of six older horses, Mercante left the gate comfortably and assumed the leading position along the rail with Kupuna tracking in the clear about a length behind. After a first quarter mile in :23.34 and the half in :47.10, Kupuna drew within a half-length of Mercante. The two matched strides and raced together as they left the final turn in 1:10.59. The battle continued down the stretch but Mercante refused to cede the lead.


“On paper he has early speed and I think everyone in the field saw that as well,” Rodriguez said. “But, he took me right to the lead and I knew he’d be tough from there. I was proud how well he fought back in the stretch to not let (Kupuna) get by. He dug in the entire way to the wire.”


Mercante, the 4-1 fourth betting choice, returned $2 mutuels of $10.12, $4.78 and $3.96. Kupuna, under Francisco Arrieta, paid $3.76 and $2.78. It was another 2 ¼ lengths back in third to Vote No under Umberto Rispoli, who paid $3.64 at odds of 6-1.


Ole Crazy Bone, Carcano and Lambeth completed the order of finish. Plensa and Teao (CHI) were scratched.


The victory for Mercante was worth $183,450 and increased his earnings to $1,292,952. He sports a record of 6-3-4 in 23 starts.


This was Mercante’s third stakes win and second at Churchill Downs. Last year at age 5, he won the $300,000 Kentucky Cup Classic over the Tapeta surface at Turfway Park and $275,000 Arlington (GIII) at Churchill Downs.


Mercante is a son of Gun Runner out of the Honour and Glory mare Caressing and was bred in Kentucky by Pollard’s CFP Thoroughbreds LLC.


RIVER CITY QUOTES


Walter Rodriguez, jockey, Mercante, winner: “It was very special to get this win today and I can’t thank (trainer) Brian (Knippenberg) and (owner) Mr. Carl Pollard enough. I know from riding him this winter at Turfway (in the Grade III TwinSpires Kentucky Cup Classic) how nice of a horse he is. He’s a very classy horse in the mornings and in the afternoon. On paper he has early speed and I think everyone in the field saw that as well. But, he took me right to the lead and I knew he’d be tough from there. I was proud how well he fought back in the stretch to not let (Kupuna) get by. He dug in the entire way to the wire.”


VIKING BOLDLY RAIDS $300,000 BET ON SUNSHINE


LOUISVILLE, Ky. (Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026) – Viking broke fast from the gate and scored a front-running 3 ¾-length victory over Jack’s Promise in Saturday’s 18th running of the $300,000 Bet On Sunshine Stakes (Listed) at Churchill Downs.


Viking clocked six furlongs on a fast track in 1:09.55 under jockey Tyler Gaffalione, who rode the winner for trainer Dave Fawkes and owners JoAnn and Alex Lieblong.


The win was worth $175,700 and the 5-year-old gelding’s record improved to 12-5-1-0—$374,758. This was the second sprinting stakes win of the year for Viking, who also wired rivals in the $100,000 Smile Sprint at Gulfstream Park.


“He’s really thrived since arriving in our barn and he showed that again today,” Fawkes said. “I think he’s a pretty good one and this race can set him up for some bigger opportunities in the future.”


Viking got away from post No. 3 in good order and surged to the front in the field of 11 3-year-olds and up through splits of :22.40, :45.36 and :57.11. Jack’s Promise tracked in second in the clear and got within a half-length down the backstretch but Viking was full of run and spurted clear in the stretch to dust the competition.


“The whole Fawkes team did a great job getting him ready today,” Gaffalione said. “I was just the passenger around there. He broke really sharp and finished up really well down the lane.”


Viking returned $9.56, $5.64 and $4.76 as the 7-2 second betting choice. Jack’s Promise, under Manny Esquivel at 17-1, paid $14.10 and $10.30. Tejano Twist finished another length back in third with Francisco Arrieta aboard and returned $10 to show at odds of 38-1.


Obliteration, the even-money favorite, was fourth and was followed by C K Wonder, Dreaminblue, Lips Say Bliss, Greenwich Village, Jimmy Rules, Echo Again and Golden Afternoon. Tap Me a Song and Yo Banana Boy were scratched.


Viking is a son of City of Light out of the Giant’s Causeway mare Justwalkonby. He was bred in Kentucky by Fred W. Hertrich III, John D. Fielding and Robert L. Tribbett.


The Bet On Sunshine is named for the 13-time stakes winning sprinter who won back-to-back runnings of the Aristides Handicap (Grade III). Trained by Paul McGee, Bet On Sunshine posted a record of 22-7-10 and $1,449,892 from 47 starts between 1995-2002 for owner David P. Holloway Racing Inc. The Florida-bred son of Big Bet finished third in the Breeders’ Cup Sprint (GI) twice behind Elmhurst and Hesabull in 1997 at Hollywood Park and behind Kona Gold and the filly Honest Lady in 2000 at Churchill Downs. He also ran in the 2001 Sprint but finished 13th. Bet On Sunshine won eight of 20 starts at Churchill Downs with four seconds and four thirds.


BET ON SUNSHINE QUOTES


Tyler Gaffalione, jockey, Viking, winner: “The whole Fawkes team did a great job getting him ready today. I was just the passenger around there. He broke really sharp and finished up really well down the lane.”


David Fawkes, trainer, Viking, winner: “He’s really thrived since arriving in our barn and he showed that again today. I think he’s a pretty good one and this race can set him up for some bigger opportunities in the future.”
